chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard a man from our companions say:

When Al-Rashid imprisoned Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them), night fell upon him. He feared that Harun might kill him. So Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) renewed his ablution, faced the Qibla, and prayed four units of prayer to Allah, the Exalted.

Then he supplicated with these supplications, saying: 'O my Master! Save me from the imprisonment of Harun and deliver me from his hand. O the Deliverer of the tree from amidst sand, mud, and water! O the Deliverer of milk from amidst excrement and blood! O the Deliverer of the child from amidst the placenta and the womb! O the Deliverer of the soul from amidst the intestines and bowels! Deliver me from the hand of Harun.'

He said: When Musa (peace be upon him) supplicated with these prayers, a black man came to Harun in his dream, holding a drawn sword. He stood over Harun's head and said: 'O Harun! Free Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), or else I will strike your throat with this sword of mine.' Harun feared his awe-inspiring presence.

Then he called the gatekeeper, who came. He said to him: 'Go to the prison and free Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him).' The gatekeeper went out and knocked on the door of the prison. The prison guard answered him. He said: 'Who is it?' He said: 'The Caliph is calling Musa ibn Ja'far, so take him out of your prison and release him.'

The guard cried out: 'O Musa! The Caliph is calling you.' Musa (peace be upon him) rose, frightened and alarmed, saying: 'He will not call me in the middle of this night unless he intends some evil for me.'
He rose weeping, sad, worried, and despairing of his life. He came to Harun while his limbs were trembling. He said: 'Peace be upon Harun.' Harun replied with peace.

Then Harun said to him: 'I swear you by Allah, did you supplicate in the middle of this night with any prayers?' He said: 'Yes.' He asked: 'What were they?' He said: 'I renewed my ablution, prayed four units to Allah the Exalted, raised my gaze to the sky and said: O my Master, deliver me from the hand of Harun and his evil.' And he mentioned to him what he had said in his supplication.

Harun said: 'Indeed Allah has accepted your prayer. O gatekeeper! Release him.' Then he ordered three robes of honor to be given to him, mounted him on his own horse, honored him, and made him his intimate companion.

Then he said: 'Recite the words,' so he taught him. He released him and handed him over to the gatekeeper to take him to his house and remain with him. Thus, Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) became a noble and respected figure with Harun.
He would visit him every Thursday until Harun imprisoned him a second time. He did not release him until he handed him over to As-Sandi ibn Shahak, who killed him with poison.
ai.seo_question: What happened between Harun al-Rashid and Musa ibn Ja'far regarding imprisonment and supplication?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual authority of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) during his imprisonment by Harun al-Rashid, illustrating how his supplication invoked divine intervention through a visionary dream. The specific titles of God used in the dua—such as 'Deliverer of the child from the womb'—emphasize God's power over creation, which Harun recognized as the cause of his release and subsequent honor. This event underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Imams' intercessory role and their enduring dignity even under political oppression.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-13 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father that he had heard one of his companions say,

“When (Harun) Ar-Rashid imprisoned Musa ibn Ja’far (s), he could not see the daytime. He feared that Harun might kill him. Then Musa ibn Ja’far (s) made ablutions again, turned his face towards the Qibla, and said four units of prayers to the Honorable the Exalted God.

Then he prayed using the following supplications.The Imam (s) said, “O my Master! Please save me from the hands of Harun. O the Savior of the trees from the midst of mud, sand (and water)! O the Savior of milk from the midst of excretions and blood !’ O the Savior of the offspring from the midst of the placenta and the uterus! O the Savior of the fire from the midst of iron and stone! O the Savior of the soul from the midst of the intestines! Save me from the hands of Harun.”

The narrator of this tradition added, “When Musa (s) said this prayer, Harun saw a black man in his dream. He had a drawn out sword in his hand. He stood over Harun’s head and said, “O Harun! Free Musa ibn Ja’far or I will chop off your head with this sword.”
Then Harun feared the black man’s awesomeness, and called in his gatekeeper. The gatekeeper came in. Harun told him, “Go to the prison and free Musa ibn Ja’far.”

The narrator of this tradition added, “Then the gatekeeper left. When he arrived at the jail he called in the prison guard. The prison guard asked, “Who is it?” The gatekeeper said, “The Caliph has called in Musa ibn Ja’far. Take him out of his cell and free him.” The prison guard said, “O Musa! The Caliph has called you in.”
Then Musa (s) got up frightened and said, “He would not call me in tonight unless he had some wicked intentions about me.”

Then he got up while he was crying and sad, worried for his life. He went to Harun while shaking. Then the Imam (s) greeted Harun and Harun greeted him back. Then Harun asked him, “I swear to you by God to tell me if you have made any supplications tonight?” The Imam (s) said, “Yes.” He asked, “What were they?” The Imam (s) said, “I made another ablution, said four units of prayers to the Honorable the Exalted God, raised my head towards the sky and said, “O my Master! Please save me from the hands of Harun and his wickedness.” The Imam (s) told him the rest of his supplications.

Then Harun said, “Indeed God accepted your prayer. O gatekeeper! Free him!” Then Harun asked for three robes of honor to be given to him, gave him his own horse, honored him and took the Imam (s) for his own bosom companion.
Harun then said, “Recite that prayer for me.” The Imam (s) taught it to him.

The narrator of the tradition added, “He freed him and had his gatekeeper accompany him to his house. From then on Musa ibn Ja’far (s) was honored and respected by Harun and went to see him every Thursday until Harun imprisoned him again. This time he did not free him until he handed him over to As-Sandi ibn Shahak who murdered him with poison.
